"""tests for council. run with: python tests/test_council.py"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from council.agent import Agent
from council.blackboard import Blackboard
from council.client import ApiError, ChatClient
from council.config import example_config, load_config
from council.patterns import debate, fanout, pipeline, supervise, vote
from council.run import RunResult, Turn, merge_usage
from council.transcript import render_transcript, to_markdown

passed = 0
failed = 0


def check(name, cond):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print("FAIL: %s" % name)


class ScriptedClient:
    """fake ChatClient.chat: responder(messages) -> (text, usage)."""

    def __init__(self, responder):
        self.responder = responder
        self.calls = []

    def chat(self, messages, model=None, temperature=None, max_tokens=None):
        self.calls.append(messages)
        text = self.responder(messages)
        return text, {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 5,
                      "total_tokens": 15}


def last_user_text(messages):
    return messages[-1]["content"]


def sys_text(messages):
    return messages[0]["content"]


# --- client over real http ---

class FakeHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    script = []  # list of (status, payload dict)

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        self.server.seen.append(json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}"))
        self.server.paths.append(self.path)
        status, payload = self.script.pop(0)
        body = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass


def start_server(script):
    FakeHandler.script = list(script)
    srv = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), FakeHandler)
    srv.seen = []
    srv.paths = []
    t = threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    return srv


def openai_payload(text):
    return {"choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": text}}],
            "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 3, "completion_tokens": 7,
                      "total_tokens": 10}}


srv = start_server([(200, openai_payload("hello there"))])
c = ChatClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:%d/v1" % srv.server_port,
               api_key="x", max_retries=0)
text, usage = c.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
check("client parses text", text == "hello there")
check("client parses usage", usage["total_tokens"] == 10)
check("client hits /v1/chat/completions",
      srv.paths == ["/v1/chat/completions"])
sent = srv.seen[0]
check("client sends model and messages",
      sent["model"] == "gpt-4o-mini" and sent["messages"][0]["content"] == "hi")
srv.shutdown()

srv = start_server([(500, {}), (200, openai_payload("recovered"))])
c = ChatClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:%d" % srv.server_port,
               api_key="x", max_retries=2)
text, _ = c.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
check("client retries 500 then succeeds", text == "recovered")
srv.shutdown()

srv = start_server([(400, {"error": "bad request"})])
c = ChatClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:%d" % srv.server_port,
               api_key="x", max_retries=2)
try:
    c.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
    check("client raises on 400", False)
except ApiError as e:
    check("client raises on 400", "400" in str(e))
srv.shutdown()

# --- agent ---

a = Agent("maya", "a pragmatic engineer", system="be terse", temperature=0.3)
check("agent system prompt has name and role",
      "maya" in a.system_prompt() and "pragmatic engineer" in a.system_prompt())
check("agent system prompt includes extra system",
      "be terse" in a.system_prompt())

seen = {}


def cap(messages):
    seen["messages"] = messages
    return "ok"


sc = ScriptedClient(cap)
a.say("do the thing", sc)
check("agent sends system then user",
      seen["messages"][0]["role"] == "system"
      and seen["messages"][1] == {"role": "user", "content": "do the thing"})
check("agent passes temperature through",
      sc.calls and True)

b = Agent.from_dict({"name": "x", "role": "r"})
check("agent from_dict defaults", b.temperature == 0.7 and b.model is None)

# --- blackboard ---

bb = Blackboard()
bb.write("plan", "step one", author="maya")
check("blackboard write/read", bb.read("plan") == "step one")
check("blackboard missing default", bb.read("nope") is None)
check("blackboard keys", bb.keys() == ["plan"])
bb.append("ideas", "a")
bb.append("ideas", "b")
check("blackboard append builds list", bb.read("ideas") == ["a", "b"])
bb.write("solo", "one")
bb.append("solo", "two")
check("blackboard append converts scalar",
      bb.read("solo") == ["one", "two"])
bb.note("a note", author="theo")
check("blackboard history records",
      len(bb.history()) == 6)
md = bb.dump_markdown()
check("blackboard markdown dump",
      "## ideas" in md and "- a" in md and "step one" in md)


def hammer(n):
    bb2 = Blackboard()

    def w(i):
        bb2.append("k", i)

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=w, args=(i,)) for i in range(n)]
    [t.start() for t in threads]
    [t.join() for t in threads]
    return bb2


bb3 = hammer(50)
check("blackboard thread safe", sorted(bb3.read("k")) == list(range(50)))

# --- debate ---

def debate_resp(messages):
    who = re.search(r"You are (\w+)", sys_text(messages)).group(1)
    body = last_user_text(messages)
    if "final verdict" in body:
        return "verdict: the debate is settled."
    rnd = re.search(r"Round (\d+)", body).group(1)
    return "%s makes point in round %s" % (who, rnd)


agents = [Agent("pro", "argue for"), Agent("con", "argue against")]
res = debate(ScriptedClient(debate_resp), "tabs or spaces?", agents, rounds=2)
check("debate turn count", len(res.turns) == 2 * 2 + 1)
check("debate verdict last",
      res.turns[-1].kind == "verdict" and "settled" in res.answer)
# real check: capture prompts
prompts = []


def cap_debate(messages):
    prompts.append(last_user_text(messages))
    return debate_resp(messages)


debate(ScriptedClient(cap_debate), "q?", agents, rounds=2)
check("later rounds include earlier transcript",
      "pro makes point in round 1" in prompts[2])
check("debate usage totals", res.usage_totals()["total_tokens"] == 5 * 15)

# --- vote ---

def vote_resp(choices):
    it = iter(choices)

    def r(messages):
        return "VOTE: %s\nbecause reasons." % next(it)
    return r


agents3 = [Agent("a1", "voter"), Agent("a2", "voter"), Agent("a3", "voter")]
res = vote(ScriptedClient(vote_resp(["x", "y", "x"])), "pick one",
           ["x", "y"], agents3)
check("vote tally", res.extra["tally"] == {"x": 2, "y": 1})
check("vote winner", res.extra["winner"] == "x")
check("vote answer names winner", "Winner: x" in res.answer)

# tie -> runoff
tie_calls = {"n": 0}


def tie_resp(messages):
    tie_calls["n"] += 1
    body = last_user_text(messages)
    if "Options:\n- x\n- y" in body or "- x\n- y" in body:
        # first round: tie
        return "VOTE: %s\ntie round." % (["x", "y"][tie_calls["n"] % 2])
    # runoff: everybody picks x
    return "VOTE: x\nrunoff decided."


res = vote(ScriptedClient(tie_resp), "pick one", ["x", "y"],
           [Agent("a1", "v"), Agent("a2", "v")])
check("vote runoff resolves tie", res.extra["winner"] == "x")


def ci_resp(messages):
    return "VOTE: ALPHA\nshouting my choice."


res = vote(ScriptedClient(ci_resp), "t", ["alpha", "beta"],
           [Agent("a1", "v")])
check("vote case insensitive", res.extra["winner"] == "alpha")


def mention_resp(messages):
    return "i think beta is clearly better, no formal vote line."


res = vote(ScriptedClient(mention_resp), "t", ["alpha", "beta"],
           [Agent("a1", "v")])
check("vote falls back to mentioned option", res.extra["winner"] == "beta")


def abstain_resp(messages):
    return "i refuse to choose, both are bad."


res = vote(ScriptedClient(abstain_resp), "t", ["alpha", "beta"],
           [Agent("a1", "v")])
check("vote abstain gives no winner", res.extra["winner"] is None)

# --- supervise ---

def sup_resp(messages):
    body = last_user_text(messages)
    if "Break this into" in body:
        return "SUBTASK: write the intro\nSUBTASK: write the outro"
    if "Subtask results" in body:
        who = re.search(r"You are (\w+)", sys_text(messages)).group(1)
        return "%s merged everything." % who
    who = re.search(r"You are (\w+)", sys_text(messages)).group(1)
    sub = re.search(r"Your subtask: (.+)", body).group(1)
    return "%s did: %s" % (who, sub)


sup = Agent("boss", "supervisor")
workers = [Agent("w1", "worker"), Agent("w2", "worker")]
res = supervise(ScriptedClient(sup_resp), "write a post", sup, workers)
check("supervise parses subtasks",
      res.extra["subtasks"] == ["write the intro", "write the outro"])
check("supervise turns", len(res.turns) == 1 + 2 + 1)
check("supervise merge last",
      res.turns[-1].kind == "merge" and "merged" in res.answer)
check("supervise worker did its subtask",
      "w1 did: write the intro" in res.turns[1].text)


def ramble_resp(messages):
    body = last_user_text(messages)
    if "Break this into" in body:
        return "hmm, lots of steps, hard to say, just do stuff"
    if "Subtask results" in body:
        return "merged anyway."
    return "did a thing"


res = supervise(ScriptedClient(ramble_resp), "do stuff",
                Agent("boss", "s"), [Agent("w1", "w")])
check("supervise falls back when no subtask lines",
      len(res.extra["subtasks"]) == 1 and res.turns[-1].kind == "merge")

# --- pipeline ---

def pipe_resp(messages):
    body = last_user_text(messages)
    who = re.search(r"You are (\w+)", sys_text(messages)).group(1)
    if "Previous step output" in body:
        prev = body.split("Previous step output:\n")[1].split("\n\nYou are")[0]
        return "%s transformed [%s]" % (who, prev.strip())
    return "%s started" % who


stages = [Agent("s1", "draft"), Agent("s2", "edit"), Agent("s3", "polish")]
res = pipeline(ScriptedClient(pipe_resp), "write it", stages)
check("pipeline final is last stage output",
      res.answer == "s3 transformed [s2 transformed [s1 started]]")
check("pipeline order", [t.speaker for t in res.turns] == ["s1", "s2", "s3"])

# --- fanout ---

def fan_resp(messages):
    body = last_user_text(messages)
    who = re.search(r"You are (\w+)", sys_text(messages)).group(1)
    if "Independent answers" in body:
        return "merged: everyone contributed."
    return "%s says hi" % who


res = fanout(ScriptedClient(fan_resp), "greet",
             [Agent("w1", "w"), Agent("w2", "w"), Agent("w3", "w")])
check("fanout turns", len(res.turns) == 4)
check("fanout merge", "merged" in res.answer)
check("fanout workers all ran",
      {t.speaker for t in res.turns[:3]} == {"w1", "w2", "w3"})

# --- run result helpers ---

r = RunResult("debate", "q")
r.add(Turn("a", "x", {"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 2,
                      "total_tokens": 3}))
r.add(Turn("b", "y", {"prompt_tokens": 4, "completion_tokens": 5,
                      "total_tokens": 9}))
check("usage totals sum", r.usage_totals() == {"prompt_tokens": 5,
      "completion_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 12})
check("merge_usage", merge_usage({"a": 1}, {"a": 2, "b": 3}) ==
      {"a": 3, "b": 3})

md = to_markdown(r.finish("done!"))
check("transcript markdown",
      "# council run: debate" in md and "task: q" in md
      and "done!" in md and "turns: 2" in md)
check("render_transcript",
      "**a:** hi" in render_transcript([("a", "hi")]))

# --- config ---

cfg = example_config()
check("example config has debate shape",
      cfg["pattern"] == "debate" and len(cfg["agents"]) == 2)
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as f:
    json.dump(cfg, f)
    path = f.name
loaded = load_config(path)
check("load_config", loaded["pattern"] == "debate"
      and loaded["judge"].name == "moderator"
      and loaded["params"]["rounds"] == 2)
os.unlink(path)

with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as f:
    json.dump({"pattern": "nope"}, f)
    bad = f.name
try:
    load_config(bad)
    check("load_config rejects bad pattern", False)
except ValueError:
    check("load_config rejects bad pattern", True)
os.unlink(bad)

try:
    load_config("/tmp/does-not-exist-council.json")
    check("load_config missing file raises", False)
except FileNotFoundError:
    check("load_config missing file raises", True)

# --- cli ---

import council.cli as cli_mod

a = cli_mod.parse_agent("maya: a pragmatic engineer")
check("parse_agent splits", a.name == "maya" and "pragmatic" in a.role)
a = cli_mod.parse_agent("solo")
check("parse_agent default role", a.name == "solo")
try:
    cli_mod.parse_agent(": noname")
    check("parse_agent rejects empty name", False)
except ValueError:
    check("parse_agent rejects empty name", True)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    old = os.getcwd()
    os.chdir(d)
    cli_mod.cmd_init(None)
    check("cli init writes council.json", os.path.exists("council.json"))
    with open("council.json") as f:
        check("cli init valid json", json.load(f)["pattern"] == "debate")
    os.chdir(old)

# cli debate end to end with scripted client
old_make = cli_mod.make_client
cli_mod.make_client = lambda args: ScriptedClient(debate_resp)
ns = cli_mod.build_parser().parse_args(
    ["debate", "tabs or spaces?", "--agent", "pro: argue for",
     "--agent", "con: argue against", "--rounds", "1", "--quiet"])
try:
    cli_mod.cmd_debate(ns)
    check("cli debate runs", True)
except Exception as e:
    print("cli debate raised: %s" % e)
    check("cli debate runs", False)
cli_mod.make_client = old_make

# --- per-agent token/cost budgets ---

from council.agent import BudgetExceeded

cheap = Agent("cheap", "a thrifty debater", budget_tokens=30)
cheap.say("go", ScriptedClient(lambda m: "short"))
check("budget accumulates tokens", cheap.tokens_used == 15)
cheap.say("go again", ScriptedClient(lambda m: "short"))
check("budget at cap still ok", cheap.tokens_used == 30)
calls = ScriptedClient(lambda m: "short")
try:
    cheap.say("one more", calls)
    check("budget exceeded raises", False)
except BudgetExceeded:
    check("budget exceeded raises", True)
check("over-budget call never hits the api", len(calls.calls) == 0)
check("budget sits exactly at cap", cheap.budget_left() == 0)

mid = Agent("mid", "crosses mid-call", budget_tokens=20)
try:
    mid.say("go", ScriptedClient(lambda m: "short"))   # 15 used
    mid.say("go", ScriptedClient(lambda m: "short"))   # 30 > 20, over
    check("mid-call overage raises", False)
except BudgetExceeded:
    check("mid-call overage raises", True)
check("mid-call overage recorded", mid.tokens_used == 30
      and mid.budget_left() == -10)

spent = Agent("spent", "already broke", budget_tokens=10)
spent.tokens_used = 10
gate = ScriptedClient(lambda m: "nope")
try:
    spent.say("go", gate)
    check("pre-spent budget refuses before api call", False)
except BudgetExceeded:
    check("pre-spent budget refuses before api call", True)
check("pre-spent refusal makes no api call", len(gate.calls) == 0)

rich = Agent("rich", "no limits here")
for _ in range(10):
    rich.say("go", ScriptedClient(lambda m: "yap " * 50))
check("no budget means no cap", rich.tokens_used == 150)

priced = Agent("priced", "knows the rates",
              prompt_price=2.0, completion_price=8.0)
priced.say("go", ScriptedClient(lambda m: "short"))
check("cost math", abs(priced.cost_used - (10 / 1000 * 2.0
                                          + 5 / 1000 * 8.0)) < 1e-9)
check("report carries budget fields",
      priced.report()["cost_used"] == round(priced.cost_used, 6))
priced.reset_budget()
check("reset_budget zeroes counters",
      priced.tokens_used == 0 and priced.cost_used == 0.0)

cfg_agent = Agent.from_dict({"name": "capped", "budget_tokens": 100,
                             "prompt_price": 1.5})
check("from_dict reads budget keys",
      cfg_agent.budget_tokens == 100 and cfg_agent.prompt_price == 1.5)

res = RunResult("debate", "q")
res.add(Turn("maya", "a", {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 5,
                           "total_tokens": 15}))
res.add(Turn("theo", "b", {"prompt_tokens": 20, "completion_tokens": 5,
                           "total_tokens": 25}))
res.add(Turn("maya", "c", {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 5,
                           "total_tokens": 15}))
per = res.spend_by_agent()
check("spend_by_agent aggregates",
      per["maya"]["total_tokens"] == 30
      and per["theo"]["total_tokens"] == 25)
md = to_markdown(res)
check("transcript shows per-agent spend",
      "maya=30" in md and "theo=25" in md)

print("\n%d passed, %d failed" % (passed, failed))
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

repos.readme:
# relay

One local endpoint in front of many model backends. relay is an
OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway: it serves `POST /v1/chat/completions`,
`POST /v1/embeddings`, and `GET /v1/models` on 127.0.0.1, then routes
each request to a configured upstream, with ordered fallbacks, circuit
breakers, per-key budgets, request logging, and a small dashboard.

Python, stdlib only. No frameworks, no dependencies, no external assets.

## quickstart

Point two fake upstreams at it. Any OpenAI-compatible server works;
`mockllm` (sibling project) is handy for this:

```bash
# terminal 1 and 2: two fake model servers
python3 mockllm.py --port 8318
python3 mockllm.py --port 8319
```

Write `relay.json`:

```json
{
  "upstreams": [
    {"name": "fast", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8318/v1", "models": ["flash"], "timeout_s": 30},
    {"name": "backup", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8319/v1", "models": ["flash"], "timeout_s": 30}
  ],
  "routes": [
    {"match": "*", "try": ["fast", "backup"]}
  ],
  "pricing": [
    {"match": "*", "in_per_1m": 0.10, "out_per_1m": 0.40}
  ]
}
```

Then:

```bash
python3 relay.py check --config relay.json
python3 relay.py serve --config relay.json --no-auth --port 8321
```

And use it like any OpenAI-compatible API:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8321/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}'
```

The response carries an `X-Relay-Upstream` header naming the upstream
that served it. Streaming works: SSE bytes pass through untouched, and
relay captures token usage from the final usage chunk when the upstream
sends one (otherwise it estimates from chars/4).

With no `relay.json` and no `--config`, relay runs a single upstream
from env: `RELAY_UPSTREAM_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8318/v1`) and
`RELAY_UPSTREAM_KEY`.

## relay.json

- `upstreams`: list of `name`, `base_url`, `api_key_env` (env var holding
  the key, optional), `models` (for `/v1/models` aggregation), `weight`
  (reserved, must be >= 0), `timeout_s` (per-request, must be > 0).
- `routes`: ordered list of `match` + `try`. Match is exact (`gpt-4o`),
  prefix (`gpt-*`), or catch-all (`*`). First matching route wins; its
  `try` list is the ordered fallback chain.
- `pricing`: list of `match` + `in_per_1m` / `out_per_1m` ($ per million
  tokens). First match wins. Cost = prompt/1M * in + completion/1M * out.
  Embeddings bill prompt tokens at the input rate.
- `log_file`: where request logs go (default `~/.relay/requests.jsonl`).
- `port`: default serve port (default 8321, `--port` overrides).

`relay check` validates the config and GETs each upstream's `/v1/models`,
printing PASS/FAIL per upstream.

## fallbacks and circuit breakers

Upstreams are tried in route order. On 429, 5xx, timeouts, or connection
errors, relay records the failure, waits a short jittered backoff, and
tries the next upstream. Other 4xx responses are forwarded to the client
as-is with no retry.

Each upstream has a circuit breaker: 3 consecutive failures trip it, and
tripped upstreams are skipped while a healthy one exists. After 30s a
tripped breaker goes half-open and allows one probe; success closes it,
failure re-opens it. If every upstream is tripped, relay still tries
them rather than failing outright. `/relay/status` shows per-upstream
breaker state, rolling average latency, and request/error counts.

## keys and budgets

By default clients must authenticate with a relay-issued key:

```bash
python3 relay.py keys add --name laptop --daily-cap 5.00
# prints rl_... exactly once. save it; it is never shown again.
python3 relay.py keys list   # names and prefixes only, never full keys
python3 relay.py keys rm --name laptop
```

Keys are stored in `~/.relay/keys.json` as salted sha256 hashes, never
plaintext. Clients send `Authorization: Bearer rl_...`.

`--daily-cap` sets a max USD spend per day from the pricing table. Once
a key reaches its cap, requests get `402` with a JSON error until the
next day. Keys without a cap are unlimited. `--no-auth` on `serve`
disables auth entirely for local dev.

## logging

Every proxied request appends one JSON line with timestamp, key name,
requested model, upstream used, fallback count, latency ms,
prompt/completion/total tokens, estimated cost, and HTTP status. Logs
rotate by size: 5 files of 10MB each.

## admin api and dashboard

- `GET /relay/status` - JSON: version, uptime, totals, per-upstream
  health/breaker/latency/counts, today's per-key spend.
- `POST /relay/reload` - re-reads relay.json without restart. Requires
  `Authorization: Bearer <admin token>` when a token is configured via
  `RELAY_ADMIN_TOKEN` or `serve --admin-token`; open when none is set.
- `GET /relay/` - dashboard: upstream table with health dots, request
  and cost counters, auto-refreshes every 5 seconds. Single HTML file,
  no frameworks.

## cli

```
relay serve [--port 8321] [--config relay.json] [--no-auth] [--admin-token ...]
relay keys add --name NAME [--daily-cap 5.00]
relay keys rm --name NAME
relay keys list
relay check [--config relay.json]
relay --version
```

The server always binds 127.0.0.1.

## layout

- `relay.py` - CLI entry
- `proxy.py` - HTTP server, proxy loop, admin endpoints
- `config.py` - relay.json loading, validation, `check` pings
- `router.py` - model pattern matching, route resolution, pricing math
- `upstream.py` - upstream state, circuit breaker, raw HTTP forwarding
- `keys.py` - key issuance/verification, daily spend caps
- `log.py` - JSONL request log with rotation
- `dashboard.py` - the dashboard HTML
- `test_relay.py` - 87 checks, run with `python3 test_relay.py`

Tests run entirely against fake upstream servers on 127.0.0.1: route
matching, fallback on 500/429/connection-refused, streaming byte
passthrough with usage capture, breaker trip and half-open recovery,
key auth and hashed storage, daily-cap 402s, pricing math, log schema
and rotation, model aggregation, config validation, and admin reload.
No real API keys, no external network.

them rather than failing outright. `/relay/status` shows per-upstream
breaker state, rolling average latency, and request/error counts.

## keys and budgets

By default clients must authenticate with a relay-issued key:

```bash
python3 relay.py keys add --name laptop --daily-cap 5.00
# prints rl_... exactly once. save it; it is never shown again.
python3 relay.py keys list   # names and prefixes only, never full keys
python3 relay.py keys rm --name laptop
```

Keys are stored in `~/.relay/keys.json` as salted sha256 hashes, never
plaintext. Clients send `Authorization: Bearer rl_...`.

`--daily-cap` sets a max USD spend per day from the pricing table. Once
a key reaches its cap, requests get `402` with a JSON error until the
next day. Keys without a cap are unlimited. `--no-auth` on `serve`
disables auth entirely for local dev.

## logging

Every proxied request appends one JSON line with timestamp, key name,
requested model, upstream used, fallback count, latency ms,
prompt/completion/total tokens, estimated cost, and HTTP status. Logs
rotate by size: 5 files of 10MB each.

## admin api and dashboard

- `GET /relay/status` - JSON: version, uptime, totals, per-upstream
  health/breaker/latency/counts, today's per-key spend.
- `POST /relay/reload` - re-reads relay.json without restart. Requires
  `Authorization: Bearer <admin token>` when a token is configured via
  `RELAY_ADMIN_TOKEN` or `serve --admin-token`; open when none is set.
- `GET /relay/` - dashboard: upstream table with health dots, request
  and cost counters, auto-refreshes every 5 seconds. Single HTML file,
  no frameworks.

## cli

```
relay serve [--port 8321] [--config relay.json] [--no-auth] [--admin-token ...]
relay keys add --name NAME [--daily-cap 5.00]
relay keys rm --name NAME
relay keys list
relay check [--config relay.json]
relay --version
```

The server always binds 127.0.0.1.

## layout

- `relay.py` - CLI entry
- `proxy.py` - HTTP server, proxy loop, admin endpoints
- `config.py` - relay.json loading, validation, `check` pings
- `router.py` - model pattern matching, route resolution, pricing math
- `upstream.py` - upstream state, circuit breaker, raw HTTP forwarding
- `keys.py` - key issuance/verification, daily spend caps
- `log.py` - JSONL request log with rotation
- `dashboard.py` - the dashboard HTML
- `test_relay.py` - 87 checks, run with `python3 test_relay.py`

Tests run entirely against fake upstream servers on 127.0.0.1: route
matching, fallback on 500/429/connection-refused, streaming byte
passthrough with usage capture, breaker trip and half-open recovery,
key auth and hashed storage, daily-cap 402s, pricing math, log schema
and rotation, model aggregation, config validation, and admin reload.
No real API keys, no external network.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# relay: openai-compatible llm gateway. see README.md for the full docs.

import argparse
import os
import sys

import config as config_mod
import keys
import proxy

VERSION = "0.1.0"


def cmd_serve(args):
    try:
        config_path, cfg = config_mod.find_config(args.config)
    except config_mod.ConfigError as e:
        print("error: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    port = args.port or cfg.get("port") or config_mod.DEFAULT_PORT
    admin_token = args.admin_token or os.environ.get("RELAY_ADMIN_TOKEN")
    auth_enabled = not args.no_auth
    server, _state = proxy.serve(cfg, config_path, port, auth_enabled, admin_token)
    print("relay %s listening on 127.0.0.1:%d" % (VERSION, port))
    print("config: %s" % (config_path or "(env default)"))
    print("auth: %s" % ("enabled" if auth_enabled else "disabled (--no-auth)"))
    print("dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:%d/relay/" % port)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    return 0


def cmd_keys_add(args):
    try:
        secret = keys.add_key(args.name, args.daily_cap)
    except ValueError as e:
        print("error: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    # printed once, never stored in plaintext
    print(secret)
    return 0


def cmd_keys_rm(args):
    if keys.remove_key(args.name):
        print("removed key '%s'" % args.name)
        return 0
    print("error: no such key '%s'" % args.name, file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


def cmd_keys_list(args):
    rows = keys.list_keys()
    if not rows:
        print("no keys")
        return 0
    print("%-20s %-12s %-10s %s" % ("name", "prefix", "daily cap", "created"))
    for r in rows:
        cap = "-" if r["daily_cap"] is None else "$%.2f" % r["daily_cap"]
        print("%-20s %-12s %-10s %s" % (r["name"], r["prefix"] + "...", cap, r["created"]))
    return 0


def cmd_check(args):
    try:
        config_path, cfg = config_mod.find_config(args.config)
    except config_mod.ConfigError as e:
        print("error: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print("config ok: %s" % (config_path or "(env default)"))
    print("%d upstream(s), %d route(s)" % (len(cfg["upstreams"]), len(cfg["routes"])))
    ok = True
    for name, passed, detail, ms in config_mod.check_upstreams(cfg):
        print("%-4s %-16s %s (%dms)" % ("PASS" if passed else "FAIL", name, detail, ms))
        ok = ok and passed
    return 0 if ok else 1


def build_parser():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="relay", description="openai-compatible llm gateway")
    p.add_argument("--version", action="version", version="relay " + VERSION)
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="command")

    s = sub.add_parser("serve", help="run the gateway")
    s.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=None)
    s.add_argument("--config", default=None, help="path to relay.json")
    s.add_argument("--no-auth", action="store_true", help="disable relay api key auth")
    s.add_argument("--admin-token", default=None, help="token for POST /relay/reload")
    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_serve)

    k = sub.add_parser("keys", help="manage relay api keys")
    ksub = k.add_subparsers(dest="keys_command")

    ka = ksub.add_parser("add", help="issue a new api key (printed once)")
    ka.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    ka.add_argument("--daily-cap", type=float, default=None, help="max usd spend per day")
    ka.set_defaults(func=cmd_keys_add)

    kr = ksub.add_parser("rm", help="revoke an api key")
    kr.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    kr.set_defaults(func=cmd_keys_rm)

    kl = ksub.add_parser("list", help="list key names and prefixes")
    kl.set_defaults(func=cmd_keys_list)

    c = sub.add_parser("check", help="validate config and ping upstreams")
    c.add_argument("--config", default=None, help="path to relay.json")
    c.set_defaults(func=cmd_check)

    return p


def main(argv=None):
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if not getattr(args, "func", None):
        build_parser().print_help()
        return 0
    return args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# relay tests: 60+ checks against fake upstreams on 127.0.0.1.
# run with: python3 test_relay.py

import http.client
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

import config as config_mod
import keys
import log as log_mod
import proxy
import router
import upstream as upstream_mod

passed = 0
failed = 0


def check(name, cond):
    global passed, failed
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1
        print("FAIL: %s" % name)


# isolate key storage from any real ~/.relay
KEYDIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="relay-test-keys-")
keys.KEY_FILE = os.path.join(KEYDIR, "keys.json")


# fake upstream servers

class FakeUpstream:
    def __init__(self, handler_fn):
        self.handler_fn = handler_fn
        self.requests = []
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        outer = self

        class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *a):
                pass

            def _run(self):
                try:
                    length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    length = 0
                body = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
                with outer.lock:
                    outer.requests.append(
                        {
                            "method": self.command,
                            "path": self.path,
                            "headers": {k.lower(): v for k, v in self.headers.items()},
                            "body": body,
                        }
                    )
                    n = len(outer.requests)
                status, payload, ctype = outer.handler_fn(n, body, self.path)
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(payload)

            do_POST = _run
            do_GET = _run

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
        self.server.daemon_threads = True
        self.port = self.server.server_address[1]
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()


def chat_payload(text="hello", prompt_t=10, completion_t=5):
    return {
        "id": "chatcmpl-x",
        "object": "chat.completion",
        "created": 1,
        "model": "m",
        "choices": [
            {
                "index": 0,
                "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                "finish_reason": "stop",
            }
        ],
        "usage": {
            "prompt_tokens": prompt_t,
            "completion_tokens": completion_t,
            "total_tokens": prompt_t + completion_t,
        },
    }


def emb_payload(prompt_t=8):
    return {
        "object": "list",
        "data": [{"object": "embedding", "index": 0, "embedding": [0.1, 0.2]}],
        "model": "m",
        "usage": {"prompt_tokens": prompt_t, "total_tokens": prompt_t},
    }


def sse_bytes(with_usage=True):
    chunks = [
        'data: {"id":"1","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"hel"},"index":0}]}',
        'data: {"id":"1","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"lo"},"index":0}]}',
    ]
    if with_usage:
        chunks.append(
            'data: {"id":"1","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[],"usage":'
            '{"prompt_tokens":10,"completion_tokens":5,"total_tokens":15}}'
        )
    chunks.append("data: [DONE]")
    return ("\n".join(chunks) + "\n").encode("utf-8")


def ok_chat(n, body, path):
    return 200, json.dumps(chat_payload()).encode(), "application/json"


def ok_models(n, body, path):
    return 200, json.dumps({"object": "list", "data": []}).encode(), "application/json"


def up_spec(name, port, models=None, key_env=None):
    d = {
        "name": name,
        "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:%d/v1" % port,
        "models": models or [],
        "weight": 1,
        "timeout_s": 5,
    }
    if key_env:
        d["api_key_env"] = key_env
    return d


def make_cfg(upstreams, routes=None, pricing=None):
    if routes is None:
        routes = [{"match": "*", "try": [u["name"] for u in upstreams]}]
    if pricing is None:
        pricing = [{"match": "*", "in_per_1m": 2.0, "out_per_1m": 4.0}]
    return {
        "upstreams": upstreams,
        "routes": routes,
        "pricing": pricing,
        "log_file": tempfile.mktemp(prefix="relay-test-log-", suffix=".jsonl"),
        "port": 8321,
    }


_servers = []


def start_relay(cfg, auth_enabled=True, admin_token=None):
    state = proxy.RelayState(cfg, None, admin_token, auth_enabled)
    logger = log_mod.RequestLogger(cfg["log_file"], max_bytes=10**9)
    handler = proxy.make_handler(state, logger)
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler)
    server.daemon_threads = True
    port = server.server_address[1]
    t = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    _servers.append(server)
    return server, port, state, logger


def http_request(port, method, path, obj=None, key=None, raw=None):
    conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=10)
    headers = {}
    if obj is not None or raw is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    if key:
        headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + key
    body = raw if raw is not None else (json.dumps(obj).encode() if obj is not None else None)
    conn.request(method, path, body=body, headers=headers)
    resp = conn.getresponse()
    data = resp.read()
    rheaders = {k.lower(): v for k, v in resp.getheaders()}
    status = resp.status
    conn.close()
    return status, rheaders, data


def last_log(logpath, timeout=5):
    # the handler thread logs after the response is sent, so poll briefly
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while True:
        try:
            with open(logpath, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                lines = [l for l in f.read().splitlines() if l.strip()]
            if lines:
                return json.loads(lines[-1])
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        if time.time() > deadline:
            raise AssertionError("no log line appeared in %s" % logpath)
        time.sleep(0.05)


def log_entries(logpath):
    with open(logpath, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return [json.loads(l) for l in f.read().splitlines() if l.strip()]


# router

routes = [
    {"match": "gpt-4o", "try": ["a"]},
    {"match": "gpt-*", "try": ["b", "c"]},
    {"match": "*", "try": ["d"]},
]
check("router exact match", router.resolve_route(routes, "gpt-4o") == ["a"])
check("router prefix match", router.resolve_route(routes, "gpt-4o-mini") == ["b", "c"])
check("router catch-all", router.resolve_route(routes, "llama-3") == ["d"])
check("router first match wins", router.resolve_route(routes, "gpt-4o") == ["a"])
check("router no match empty", router.resolve_route([{"match": "zzz", "try": ["a"]}], "gpt-4o") == [])
check("router prefix does not match mid-string", router.resolve_route(routes, "xgpt-4") == ["d"])
check("router star matches everything", router.match_pattern("*", "anything-at-all"))
check("router try order preserved", router.resolve_route(routes, "gpt-x") == ["b", "c"])

# config validation

good = {
    "upstreams": [{"name": "a", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:1/v1", "models": ["m"]}],
    "routes": [{"match": "*", "try": ["a"]}],
    "pricing": [{"match": "*", "in_per_1m": 1.0, "out_per_1m": 2.0}],
}
check("config valid passes", config_mod.validate(good) == [])
bad = dict(good, upstreams=[])
check("config empty upstreams fails", len(config_mod.validate(bad)) > 0)
dup = dict(good, upstreams=good["upstreams"] + [{"name": "a", "base_url": "http://x/v1"}])
check("config duplicate names fails", any("duplicate" in e for e in config_mod.validate(dup)))
badroute = dict(good, routes=[{"match": "*", "try": ["nope"]}])
check("config unknown upstream fails", len(config_mod.validate(badroute)) > 0)
badurl = dict(good, upstreams=[{"name": "a", "base_url": "ftp://x/v1"}])
check("config bad base_url fails", len(config_mod.validate(badurl)) > 0)
badtimeout = dict(good, upstreams=[{"name": "a", "base_url": "http://x/v1", "timeout_s": 0}])
check("config zero timeout fails", len(config_mod.validate(badtimeout)) > 0)
badprice = dict(good, pricing=[{"match": "*", "in_per_1m": -1.0}])
check("config negative pricing fails", len(config_mod.validate(badprice)) > 0)
emptytry = dict(good, routes=[{"match": "*", "try": []}])
check("config empty try fails", len(config_mod.validate(emptytry)) > 0)
envcfg = config_mod.config_from_env()
check(
    "config env default single upstream",
    len(envcfg["upstreams"]) == 1 and envcfg["routes"] == [{"match": "*", "try": ["default"]}],
)

# pricing

pricing = [
    {"match": "gpt-4o", "in_per_1m": 5.0, "out_per_1m": 15.0},
    {"match": "gpt-*", "in_per_1m": 1.0, "out_per_1m": 2.0},
    {"match": "*", "in_per_1m": 0.5, "out_per_1m": 0.5},
]
check("pricing exact pattern", router.price_for(pricing, "gpt-4o") == (5.0, 15.0))
check("pricing prefix pattern", router.price_for(pricing, "gpt-4o-mini") == (1.0, 2.0))
check(
    "pricing cost math",
    abs(router.cost_usd(pricing, "gpt-4o-mini", 1_000_000, 1_000_000) - 3.0) < 1e-9,
)

# basic proxy

up_a = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)
cfg = make_cfg([up_spec("a", up_a.port, models=["m1"])])
srv, port, state, logger = start_relay(cfg, auth_enabled=True)
secret = keys.add_key("tester-%d" % port, None)
status, headers, data = http_request(
    port, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions",
    {"model": "m1", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}, key=secret,
)
check("proxy chat 200", status == 200)
check("proxy X-Relay-Upstream header", headers.get("x-relay-upstream") == "a")
check("proxy body matches upstream", json.loads(data)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] == "hello")
status, _, _ = http_request(
    port, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions",
    {"model": "m1", "messages": []},
)
check("proxy auth missing rejected", status == 401)
status, _, data = http_request(
    port, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions",
    {"model": "m1", "messages": []}, key="rl_bogus",
)
check("proxy bad key rejected", status == 401)

# no route and bad json

cfg2 = make_cfg([up_spec("a", up_a.port)], routes=[{"match": "aaa*", "try": ["a"]}])
srv2, port2, _, _ = start_relay(cfg2, auth_enabled=False)
status, _, data = http_request(port2, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "zzz", "messages": []})
check("proxy no route 400", status == 400 and b"no route" in data)
status, _, _ = http_request(port2, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions", raw=b"not json{")
check("proxy bad json 400", status == 400)

# fallback: 500 then success

def fail500_then_ok(n, body, path):
    if n == 1:
        return 500, b"boom", "text/plain"
    return ok_chat(n, body, path)

up_b1 = FakeUpstream(fail500_then_ok)
up_b2 = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)
cfg3 = make_cfg(
    [up_spec("a", up_b1.port), up_spec("b", up_b2.port)],
    routes=[{"match": "*", "try": ["a", "b"]}],
)
srv3, port3, state3, _ = start_relay(cfg3, auth_enabled=False)
status, headers, data = http_request(
    port3, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "m", "messages": []}
)
check("fallback 500 then success", status == 200)
check("fallback header names second upstream", headers.get("x-relay-upstream") == "b")
entry = last_log(cfg3["log_file"])
check("fallback count logged", entry["fallbacks"] == 1 and entry["upstream"] == "b")

# fallback: 429 then success

def fail429_then_ok(n, body, path):
    if n == 1:
        return 429, b"slow down", "text/plain"
    return ok_chat(n, body, path)

up_c1 = FakeUpstream(fail429_then_ok)
up_c2 = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)
cfg4 = make_cfg(
    [up_spec("a", up_c1.port), up_spec("b", up_c2.port)],
    routes=[{"match": "*", "try": ["a", "b"]}],
)
srv4, port4, _, _ = start_relay(cfg4, auth_enabled=False)
status, headers, _ = http_request(port4, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "m", "messages": []})
check("fallback 429 then success", status == 200 and headers.get("x-relay-upstream") == "b")

# fallback: connection refused then success

import socket

s = socket.socket()
s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
dead_port = s.getsockname()[1]
s.close()
up_d2 = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)
cfg5 = make_cfg(
    [up_spec("dead", dead_port), up_spec("b", up_d2.port)],
    routes=[{"match": "*", "try": ["dead", "b"]}],
)
srv5, port5, _, _ = start_relay(cfg5, auth_enabled=False)
status, headers, _ = http_request(port5, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "m", "messages": []})
check("fallback conn refused then success", status == 200 and headers.get("x-relay-upstream") == "b")

# all fail -> 502

cfg6 = make_cfg([up_spec("dead", dead_port)], routes=[{"match": "*", "try": ["dead"]}])
srv6, port6, _, _ = start_relay(cfg6, auth_enabled=False)
status, _, data = http_request(port6, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "m", "messages": []})
check("proxy all fail 502", status == 502 and b"error" in data)

# upstream 400 forwarded without retry

def always400(n, body, path):
    return 400, json.dumps({"error": {"message": "bad request"}}).encode(), "application/json"

up_e = FakeUpstream(always400)
up_e2 = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)
cfg7 = make_cfg(
    [up_spec("a", up_e.port), up_spec("b", up_e2.port)],
    routes=[{"match": "*", "try": ["a", "b"]}],
)
srv7, port7, _, _ = start_relay(cfg7, auth_enabled=False)
status, headers, data = http_request(port7, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "m", "messages": []})
check("proxy 400 forwarded as-is", status == 400 and b"bad request" in data)
check("proxy 400 no retry", len(up_e.requests) == 1 and len(up_e2.requests) == 0)
check("proxy 400 keeps upstream header", headers.get("x-relay-upstream") == "a")

# streaming

def sse_ok(n, body, path):
    return 200, sse_bytes(with_usage=True), "text/event-stream"

def sse_no_usage(n, body, path):
    return 200, sse_bytes(with_usage=False), "text/event-stream"

up_s = FakeUpstream(sse_ok)
cfg8 = make_cfg([up_spec("a", up_s.port)])
srv8, port8, _, _ = start_relay(cfg8, auth_enabled=False)
status, headers, data = http_request(
    port8, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions",
    {"model": "m", "messages": [], "stream": True},
)
check("stream 200 event-stream", status == 200 and headers.get("content-type") == "text/event-stream")
check("stream bytes passthrough untouched", data == sse_bytes(with_usage=True))
entry = last_log(cfg8["log_file"])
check(
    "stream usage captured",
    entry["prompt_tokens"] == 10 and entry["completion_tokens"] == 5,
)

up_s2 = FakeUpstream(sse_no_usage)
cfg9 = make_cfg([up_spec("a", up_s2.port)])
srv9, port9, _, _ = start_relay(cfg9, auth_enabled=False)
status, _, _ = http_request(
    port9, "POST", "/v1/chat/completions",
    {"model": "m", "messages": [], "stream": True},
)
entry = last_log(cfg9["log_file"])
check("stream no usage estimated", entry["completion_tokens"] > 0 and entry["prompt_tokens"] >= 1)

# embeddings

def ok_emb(n, body, path):
    return 200, json.dumps(emb_payload()).encode(), "application/json"

up_emb = FakeUpstream(ok_emb)
cfg10 = make_cfg([up_spec("a", up_emb.port)])
srv10, port10, _, _ = start_relay(cfg10, auth_enabled=False)
status, headers, data = http_request(
    port10, "POST", "/v1/embeddings", {"model": "e", "input": "hello world"}
)
check("embeddings proxied", status == 200 and b"embedding" in data)

status, _, data = http_request(port12, "GET", "/relay/status")

check(
    "status keys spend visible",
    any(k["spend_usd"] > 0 for k in obj["keys_today"]),
)

cfgpath = tempfile.mktemp(prefix="relay-cfg-", suffix=".json")
up_r1 = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)
up_r2 = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)

check("reload applied new route", headers.get("x-relay-upstream") == "b")

status, headers, data = http_request(rport, "GET", "/relay/")
check(
    "dashboard html served",

)

up_chk = FakeUpstream(ok_models)
chk_cfg = make_cfg([up_spec("chk", up_chk.port)])
results = config_mod.check_upstreams(chk_cfg)
check("check_upstreams pass", results[0][1] is True and results[0][2] == "ok")

up_k = FakeUpstream(ok_chat)
cfgk = make_cfg([up_spec("a", up_k.port)])

# version

out = subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "relay.py", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
)
check("cli version", out.stdout.strip() == "relay 0.1.0")

# cleanup

for s_ in _servers:
    try:
        s_.shutdown()
        s_.server_close()
    except Exception:
        pass
for u in (up_a, up_b1, up_b2, up_c1, up_c2, up_d2, up_e, up_e2, up_s, up_s2, up_emb,
          up_m1, up_m2, up_f1, up_f2, up_g, up_h, up_cap, up_r1, up_r2, up_chk, up_k):
    try:
        u.close()
    except Exception:
        pass

print("%d passed, %d failed" % (passed, failed))
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# relay upstream: per-upstream state, circuit breaker, raw http forwarding.

import http.client
import os
import threading
import time
import urllib.parse

FAILURES_TO_TRIP = 3
HALF_OPEN_AFTER_S = 30.0
LATENCY_WINDOW = 50


class UpstreamError(Exception):
    # transport-level failure or retryable http status
    def __init__(self, message, retryable=True):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.retryable = retryable


class UpstreamState:
    def __init__(self, spec):
        self.name = spec["name"]
        self.base_url = spec["base_url"].rstrip("/")
        self.api_key_env = spec.get("api_key_env")
        self.models = list(spec.get("models", []))
        self.weight = spec.get("weight", 1)
        self.timeout_s = float(spec.get("timeout_s", 30))
        self.half_open_after = HALF_OPEN_AFTER_S
        self.lock = threading.RLock()  # reentrant: snapshot calls breaker_state
        self.consecutive_failures = 0
        self.total_requests = 0
        self.total_errors = 0
        self.latencies = []
        self.breaker_open = False
        self.breaker_opened_at = 0.0

    def api_key(self):
        # resolved per request so env changes apply without restart
        if self.api_key_env:
            return os.environ.get(self.api_key_env)
        return None

    def breaker_allows(self, now=None):
        # closed breakers always allow; open ones allow a probe after cooldown
        now = time.monotonic() if now is None else now
        with self.lock:
            if not self.breaker_open:
                return True
            return now - self.breaker_opened_at >= self.half_open_after

    def breaker_state(self, now=None):
        now = time.monotonic() if now is None else now
        with self.lock:
            if not self.breaker_open:
                return "closed"
            if now - self.breaker_opened_at >= self.half_open_after:
                return "half-open"
            return "open"

    def record_success(self, latency_ms):
        # any success closes the breaker, including half-open probes
        with self.lock:
            self.consecutive_failures = 0
            self.breaker_open = False
            self.total_requests += 1
            self.latencies.append(latency_ms)
            if len(self.latencies) > LATENCY_WINDOW:
                self.latencies.pop(0)

    def record_client_error(self, latency_ms):
        # upstream answered 4xx: counts as a request, never trips the breaker
        with self.lock:
            self.total_requests += 1
            self.latencies.append(latency_ms)
            if len(self.latencies) > LATENCY_WINDOW:
                self.latencies.pop(0)

    def record_failure(self):
        with self.lock:
            self.consecutive_failures += 1
            self.total_requests += 1
            self.total_errors += 1
            if self.consecutive_failures >= FAILURES_TO_TRIP:
                self.breaker_open = True
                self.breaker_opened_at = time.monotonic()

    def avg_latency_ms(self):
        with self.lock:
            if not self.latencies:
                return 0.0
            return sum(self.latencies) / len(self.latencies)

    def snapshot(self):
        # plain dict for the status endpoint
        with self.lock:
            lat = list(self.latencies)
            return {
                "name": self.name,
                "base_url": self.base_url,
                "models": list(self.models),
                "breaker": self.breaker_state(),
                "consecutive_failures": self.consecutive_failures,
                "avg_latency_ms": round(sum(lat) / len(lat), 1) if lat else 0.0,
                "requests": self.total_requests,
                "errors": self.total_errors,
            }


def post_raw(state, path, body, timeout=None):
    # returns (status, headers, response, conn); caller reads and closes conn.
    # raises UpstreamError on transport failure.
    parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(state.base_url)
    host = parsed.hostname
    port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme == "https" else 80)
    conn_cls = http.client.HTTPSConnection if parsed.scheme == "https" else http.client.HTTPConnection
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"}
    key = state.api_key()
    if key:
        headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + key
    full_path = (parsed.path or "") + path
    try:
        conn = conn_cls(host, port, timeout=timeout if timeout is not None else state.timeout_s)
        conn.request("POST", full_path, body=body, headers=headers)
        resp = conn.getresponse()
        status = resp.status
        rheaders = {k.lower(): v for k, v in resp.getheaders()}
        return status, rheaders, resp, conn
    except (OSError, http.client.HTTPException, TimeoutError) as e:
        raise UpstreamError("%s: %s" % (type(e).__name__, e), retryable=True)
    except Exception as e:
        raise UpstreamError("%s: %s" % (type(e).__name__, e), retryable=True)

# probe

score a model on benchmark prompts. point it at any openai-compatible
chat completions api, hand it a json file of evals, get a pass/fail table.

## run

```
python main.py --evals example_evals.json
python main.py --model gpt-4o --base-url http://localhost:8000/v1 --evals my_evals.json
```

flags can also come from env: `PROBE_MODEL`, `PROBE_BASE_URL`, `PROBE_API_KEY`,
`PROBE_TIMEOUT`.
exits 0 if everything passes, 1 if anything fails, 2 on bad input.

more flags:

- `--timeout SECONDS` - per-request timeout, default 120. a request that
  takes longer marks its eval failed with a timeout error.
- `--jobs N` - run N evals in parallel, default 1. output order always
  matches the evals file order.
- `--json` - print machine-readable json instead of the pass/fail table.

output looks like:

```
python reverse string       PASS
follow one-word instruction FAIL
3/4 passed
```

## writing evals

a json list. each eval needs a name, a prompt (or a full messages list,
plus an optional system prompt), and a check:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "one word answer",
    "system": "answer in one word",
    "prompt": "what is 2 + 2?",
    "check": {"type": "exact", "value": "4"}
  },
  {
    "name": "mentions recursion",
    "prompt": "explain quicksort briefly",
    "check": {"type": "contains", "value": "recursi"}
  },
  {
    "name": "version format",
    "prompt": "what python version added f-strings? just the number",
    "check": {"type": "regex", "value": "^\\s*3\\.6(\\.\\d+)?\\s*$"}
  }
]
```

check types: `contains` (substring), `exact` (whole reply, trimmed),
`regex` (re.search on the reply).

## multi-turn evals

an eval can use `turns` instead of `prompt`/`messages`: a list of user
messages sent one at a time, each with the full conversation history so
far. the check applies to the final reply.

```json
[
  {
    "name": "remembers the topic",
    "system": "you are a helpful assistant",
    "turns": ["i like blue", "what color did i just mention?"],
    "check": {"type": "contains", "value": "blue"}
  }
]
```

## notes

- stdlib only, no install
- one request per eval, sequential unless --jobs is raised
- api errors and timeouts mark that eval failed instead of crashing the run

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

from client import ChatClient
from evals import load_evals
from runner import run_evals


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="score a model on benchmark prompts")
    p.add_argument("--model", default=os.environ.get("PROBE_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini"))
    p.add_argument("--base-url", default=os.environ.get("PROBE_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1"))
    p.add_argument("--api-key", default=os.environ.get("PROBE_API_KEY", os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "")))
    p.add_argument("--evals", default="example_evals.json")
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float,
                   default=float(os.environ.get("PROBE_TIMEOUT", "120")),
                   help="seconds per api request (default 120)")
    p.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=1,
                   help="evals to run in parallel (default 1)")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true",
                   help="print machine-readable json instead of the table")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if args.jobs < 1:
        p.error("--jobs must be at least 1")
    if args.timeout <= 0:
        p.error("--timeout must be positive")

    try:
        evals = load_evals(args.evals)
    except (ValueError, OSError) as e:
        print("probe: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    client = ChatClient(args.base_url, args.api_key, args.model, timeout=args.timeout)
    results = run_evals(evals, client, jobs=args.jobs)
    passed = sum(1 for r in results if r["passed"])

    if args.json:
        out = {
            "model": args.model,
            "passed": passed,
            "total": len(results),
            "results": [
                {
                    "name": r["name"],
                    "passed": r["passed"],
                    "ms": r["ms"],
                    **({"reply": r["reply"]} if "reply" in r else {}),
                    **({"error": r["error"]} if "error" in r else {}),
                }
                for r in results
            ],
        }
        print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
        return 0 if passed == len(results) else 1

    width = max(len(r["name"]) for r in results)
    for r in results:
        print("%-*s  %s" % (width, r["name"], "PASS" if r["passed"] else "FAIL"))
        if not r["passed"] and "error" in r:
            print("    error: %s" % r["error"])

    print("%d/%d passed" % (passed, len(results)))
    return 0 if passed == len(results) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from checks import run_check
from evals import load_evals

passed = failed = 0


def check(name, cond):
    global passed, failed
    print(("ok   " if cond else "FAIL ") + name)
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1


# check types, no server needed
check("contains hit", run_check({"type": "contains", "value": "recurs"}, "it recurses"))
check("contains miss", not run_check({"type": "contains", "value": "zzz"}, "it recurses"))

        pass

        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()

    def log_message(self, *a):

delay = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), DelayHandler)

p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "main.py", "--evals", jobs_path, "--jobs", "0"],
                   capture_output=True, text=True, env=env,
                   cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
check("--jobs 0 rejected", p.returncode == 2)

# --json: machine-readable output
server3 = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)

repos.readme:
# promptlab

run one prompt against a few different system prompts (or models) and
compare the answers side by side. made for tuning agent system prompts:
tweak the prompt, rerun, see which version behaves better.

## usage

```
python promptlab.py \
  --system "you are terse. answer in one sentence." \
  --system @prompts/verbose.txt \
  --prompt "explain recursion"
```

prints each reply under a labeled section, with per-reply timing:

```
--- system 1 (gpt-4o-mini) [812ms] ---
...
```

flags:

- `--system` - a system prompt string, or @path/to/file. repeat it to compare more.
- `--model` - model name, repeatable. defaults to gpt-4o-mini.
- `--prompt` - the user prompt. leave it out and pipe one on stdin instead.
- `--base-url` - api base (default: https://api.openai.com/v1, or OPENAI_BASE_URL)
- `--api-key` - defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY
- `--json` - print machine-readable json (prompt plus a runs list with
  system, model, ms, reply) instead of labeled sections.
- `--save FILE` - write the comparison to a markdown file as well.

works with any openai-compatible chat completions endpoint. single file,
stdlib only, no install.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""run one prompt against several system prompts / models and compare."""

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
import urllib.error


def complete(base_url, api_key, model, messages, timeout):
    body = {"model": model, "messages": messages}
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        base_url.rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Authorization": "Bearer " + api_key,
        },
        method="POST",
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            payload = json.load(resp)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        detail = e.read().decode(errors="replace")[:300]
        raise RuntimeError("api error %d: %s" % (e.code, detail))
    return payload["choices"][0]["message"].get("content") or ""


# @path loads the system prompt from a file
def load_system(arg):
    if arg.startswith("@"):
        path = arg[1:]
        try:
            with open(path) as f:
                return f.read()
        except OSError:
            sys.exit("promptlab: cant read %s" % path)
    return arg


def read_prompt(arg):
    if arg:
        return arg
    if sys.stdin.isatty():
        sys.exit("promptlab: no prompt given, use --prompt or pipe one in")
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip()
    if not data:
        sys.exit("promptlab: no prompt given, use --prompt or pipe one in")
    return data


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="run one prompt against several system prompts and compare")
    p.add_argument("--system", action="append", default=[],
                   help="system prompt, or @path/to/file (repeatable)")
    p.add_argument("--model", action="append", default=[],
                   help="model name (repeatable, default: gpt-4o-mini)")
    p.add_argument("--prompt", help="user prompt (or pipe it on stdin)")
    p.add_argument("--base-url",
                   default=os.environ.get("OPENAI_BASE_URL",
                                          "https://api.openai.com/v1"))
    p.add_argument("--api-key",
                   default=os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", ""))
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=120)
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true",
                   help="print machine-readable json instead of labeled sections")
    p.add_argument("--save", metavar="FILE",
                   help="write the comparison to a markdown file")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)

    if not args.system:
        p.error("need at least one --system")

    systems = [load_system(s) for s in args.system]
    models = args.model or ["gpt-4o-mini"]
    prompt = read_prompt(args.prompt)

    # one run per system x model pair, timed
    runs = []
    for i, system in enumerate(systems, 1):
        for model in models:
            start = time.perf_counter()
            try:
                reply = complete(args.base_url, args.api_key, model,
                                 [{"role": "system", "content": system},
                                  {"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                                 args.timeout)
            except (RuntimeError, urllib.error.URLError) as e:
                reply = "error: %s" % e
            ms = int((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
            runs.append({"system": i, "model": model, "ms": ms, "reply": reply})

    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"prompt": prompt, "runs": runs}, indent=2))
    else:
        print("prompt: %s\n" % prompt)
        for run in runs:
            print("--- system %d (%s) [%dms] ---" % (run["system"], run["model"], run["ms"]))
            print(run["reply"] + "\n")

    if args.save:
        lines = ["# promptlab comparison", "", "prompt: %s" % prompt, ""]
        for run in runs:
            lines.append("## system %d (%s) - %dms" % (run["system"], run["model"], run["ms"]))
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(run["reply"])
            lines.append("")
        try:
            with open(args.save, "w") as f:
                f.write("\n".join(lines))
        except OSError as e:
            sys.exit("promptlab: cant write %s: %s" % (args.save, e))
        if not args.json:
            print("saved to %s" % args.save)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

passed = failed = 0


def check(name, cond):
    global passed, failed
    print(("ok   " if cond else "FAIL ") + name)
    if cond:
        passed += 1
    else:
        failed += 1


# fake openai-compatible server, echoes the system prompt back
class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        system = [m for m in body["messages"] if m["role"] == "system"][0]["content"]
        reply = "system was: " + system
        payload = {"choices": [{"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": reply}}]}
        data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass


server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d/v1" % server.server_port
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def run_lab(args, stdin_data=None):
    env = dict(os.environ, OPENAI_BASE_URL=base, OPENAI_API_KEY="test")
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "promptlab.py"] + args,
                          capture_output=True, text=True, env=env,
                          input=stdin_data, cwd=HERE)


# text mode: labeled sections with per-reply timing
p = run_lab(["--system", "terse", "--system", "verbose", "--prompt", "hi"])
check("text mode exits 0", p.returncode == 0)
check("two labeled sections",
      "--- system 1 (gpt-4o-mini)" in p.stdout and "--- system 2 (gpt-4o-mini)" in p.stdout)
check("timing on each reply",
      len(re.findall(r"\[(\d+)ms\]", p.stdout)) == 2)
check("replies shown", "system was: terse" in p.stdout and "system was: verbose" in p.stdout)
check("prompt echoed", "prompt: hi" in p.stdout)

# multiple models multiply the runs
p = run_lab(["--system", "s", "--model", "m1", "--model", "m2", "--prompt", "hi"])
sections = re.findall(r"--- system \d+ \((\w+)\) \[\d+ms\] ---", p.stdout)
check("two models compared", sections == ["m1", "m2"])

# --json: machine-readable
p = run_lab(["--system", "terse", "--prompt", "hi", "--json"])
doc = json.loads(p.stdout)
check("json parses", isinstance(doc, dict))
check("json has prompt", doc.get("prompt") == "hi")
check("json runs shape",
      len(doc["runs"]) == 1
      and doc["runs"][0]["system"] == 1
      and doc["runs"][0]["model"] == "gpt-4o-mini"
      and isinstance(doc["runs"][0]["ms"], int)
      and doc["runs"][0]["reply"] == "system was: terse")

# --save: markdown file
out = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".md", delete=False)
out.close()
p = run_lab(["--system", "terse", "--system", "verbose", "--prompt", "hi", "--save", out.name])
check("save exits 0", p.returncode == 0)
md = open(out.name).read()
check("markdown header", "# promptlab comparison" in md)
check("markdown prompt", "prompt: hi" in md)
check("markdown sections",
      "## system 1 (gpt-4o-mini)" in md and "## system 2 (gpt-4o-mini)" in md)
check("markdown has timing", re.search(r"## system 1 \(gpt-4o-mini\) - \d+ms", md) is not None)
check("markdown has replies", "system was: terse" in md and "system was: verbose" in md)

# --json plus --save: stdout stays pure json, file still markdown
out2 = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".md", delete=False)
out2.close()
p = run_lab(["--system", "s", "--prompt", "hi", "--json", "--save", out2.name])
doc = json.loads(p.stdout)
check("json stdout pure with save", doc["prompt"] == "hi")
check("markdown still written", "# promptlab comparison" in open(out2.name).read())

# prompt from stdin
p = run_lab(["--system", "s"], stdin_data="piped question\n")
check("stdin prompt works", "prompt: piped question" in p.stdout)

# @file system prompt
sf = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".txt", delete=False)
sf.write("from file")
sf.close()
p = run_lab(["--system", "@" + sf.name, "--prompt", "hi"])
check("@file system loads", "system was: from file" in p.stdout)

# missing system is an error
p = run_lab(["--prompt", "hi"])
check("no system rejected", p.returncode != 0)

server.shutdown()

print("\n%d passed, %d failed" % (passed, failed))
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

# mockllm

A scriptable fake OpenAI-compatible chat completions server for testing
agents. Every agent project hand-rolls a fake model server in its tests;
this is the reusable one. Stdlib only, no dependencies, no API keys,
no external network. It binds 127.0.0.1 only.

## quick start

```sh
python3 mockllm.py --port 8471
```

With no scenario it runs in echo mode: it replies with a description of
what it received (message count, last message, tools offered). Handy for
quick manual checks.

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8471/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"mockllm","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

`GET /v1/models` lists the configured model id.

## scripted scenarios

Pass `--scenario FILE` with a JSON file holding an ordered list of steps.
Each step is served in order:

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "reply": "Let me look that up.",
      "tool_calls": [
        {"name": "read_file", "arguments": {"path": "main.py"}}
      ]
    },
    {"reply": "The file has 42 lines."},
    {"error": {"status": 429, "message": "slow down", "once": true}},
    {"reply": "Done.", "latency_ms": 250}
  ]
}
```

Step kinds:

- `{"reply": "text"}` serves a plain assistant reply, then advances.
- `{"reply": ["a", "b"]}` picks one reply at random (`--seed` makes it
  deterministic).
- `{"tool_calls": [{"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}]}` serves an
  assistant message with OpenAI-style tool calls. The scenario stays on
  this step until the client sends tool results back (messages with
  `"role": "tool"`), then it advances. A step can combine `reply` text
  and `tool_calls`.
- `{"latency_ms": 250}` on any step sleeps before replying.
- `{"error": {"status": 500}}` replies with that HTTP status and an
  OpenAI-style error body, and repeats on every request. Add
  `"once": true` to serve the error a single time and then continue.
  Use `"body": {...}` to send a custom error payload verbatim.

When the steps run out, the server falls back to echo mode.

## streaming

Send `"stream": true` in the request and mockllm answers with
server-sent events instead of json: one chunk per word, a final
chunk carrying `finish_reason`, then `data: [DONE]`. Tool calls
stream as a single delta chunk with `finish_reason: tool_calls`.
Errors still come back as plain json, same as real APIs.

```sh
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8471/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"mockllm","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}'
```

## cli

```sh
python3 mockllm.py [--port N] [--scenario FILE] [--record FILE]
                   [--latency MS] [--seed N] [--model NAME]
```

- `--port` default 8471.
- `--record FILE` appends every chat request body as one JSON object
  per line (jsonl) for later inspection.
- `--latency MS` adds a default artificial delay to every reply.
- `--seed N` seeds the random choices so runs are reproducible.
- `--model NAME` sets the model id reported in replies (default
  `mockllm`).

## testing

```sh
python3 test_mockllm.py
```

Spins up the real server on localhost and checks scripted replies,
tool call sequences, error injection, latency, request recording,
and seeded determinism.
